entries.u: the default for any held beat (titles, product, quotes): the frame is never dead; the move tells the viewer where to look
sync the picture to the music: every kick/snare/word-slam gets a 0.2 s scale pop and a short shake; this single trick makes any scene feel "edited to the beat"
make 2D/3D feel photographed (documentary, UI-as-reality); a Dutch tilt (3–8°) adds unease or energy
a fast sideways move between two beats — the camera "snaps" to the next scene; stronger than a slide, cheaper than any 3D
freeze-ish emphasis (the moment a ball hits, a logo lands, a word slams) — run at 100 %, ramp to 15–30 % for ~0.4 s, ramp back; sells weight like nothing else
illustrated/flat scenes that need depth: landscapes, skylines, paper-cut worlds, title cards over layered art
the standard 3D hero move: slow orbit + slight rise + slight push; reveals reflections changing on chrome/gold/glass, which is what makes 3D look 3D
a moment of realisation, "the world changes around the subject", tension; the subject stays the same size while the background stretches

entries.t: Pull focus from near to far
entries.u: direct attention without cutting: first the foreground object is sharp, then the focus slides to the one behind it (and the story with it)

entries.t: Fly through a path of gates
entries.u: journeys and progress ("step 1 → 2 → 3"), levels, tunnels with turns; a camera path you can author with five points

entries.t: Rise from the floor to reveal
entries.u: opening reveals of a title/logo/product: start low (floor-level, looking up, object looming) and rise while the camera tilts down onto it
skip the "what colours?" detour; each line is `name: bg · base · accent · accent2 · light` and the mood it carries

entries.t: Derive a palette from one colour
entries.u: the client gave one brand colour
unify scenes; set once on the global `Stage.look`
backgrounds and fills; the cheap-gradient look comes from 2 stops, high saturation and banding

entries.t: One grid for picture and sound
entries.u: decide BPM first (110–128 for modern/tech, 90–100 for calm/Persian 6/8 feel, 140+ for sport/energy), then express every cue as bars/beats: `t = bar·4B`
showreels, social cuts, logo-driven pieces
product/feature explainers
brand films, product stories, narrated pieces
every film. Equal cut lengths are what slideshows are made of
lists of benefits, build-ups, jokes, reveals

every object move: it should pull back a little before it launches (anticipation), overshoot its target (`E.outBack`, `K.slam`), then settle (`K.spring`). This is the difference between "moves" and "feels alive"

entries.t: Contrast in scale, speed, colour and sound
entries.u: when a scene feels flat: increase contrast somewhere, not everywhere
any scene: three layers moving at different speeds make 2D feel like space
a cut where an object leaves right and the next scene's object enters from the left feels smooth; reversing direction feels like a collision (use deliberately)

entries.t: How long text stays on screen
entries.u: every piece of on-screen text
the cheapest upgrade: a sound for each visual accent
premium/calm styles; any moment that must be read
social delivery: render 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 from the same page (`--w --h`)

entries.t: A loop with no seam (reels, GIFs, backgrounds, end cards)
entries.u: anything that repeats — a social reel that auto-loops, a background under a long title, a "hold" at the end of a film. A loop that you can not find the seam in feels expensive; a pop at the seam feels broken

any everyday motion-graphics job: write `scenes` with `at` times on beats (0.5 s grid at 120 BPM), one idea per shot (`hit`, `fact`, `words`), 1–2 s each — 9–12 shots for a 15 s film — with a longer opener and a last image that holds ≥ 1.5

entries.t: Scenes that travel: whip, push, zoom, iris, blinds
entries.u: the default way to change scene in a motion-graphics film: both scenes stay visible while the camera travels (`"transition": "whip"` in the spec; `push` in vertical films, `iris` opens the next scene inside a circle from the carried object,

entries.t: One object that travels through the whole film
entries.u: any film with three or more scenes: ONE shape (an avatar, the logo mark, an icon disc) lives above the scenes and moves, resizes, changes colour and content between them (`spec.carry` with `keys`) — it turns a deck of slides into one contin

entries.t: Shots, not slides: one idea per second or two
entries.u: every list of things in a motion-graphics film — three skills, three numbers, speakers, menu items, steps, features: give each its own shot of 1–1.5 s (`hit` for a word or phrase, `fact` for a number) instead of a heading above three cards;

entries.t: Islamic star pattern grows from the centre
entries.u: Persian/Islamic visual identity, "knowledge/tradition meets technology" stories, premium backgrounds and end cards; the pattern is mathematically exact, so it looks hand-crafted
ornamental centrepieces, loading/"thinking" visuals, logo halos, meditation/intelligence metaphors
elegant "drawing itself" backgrounds, maths/engineering/art tones, a hypnotic idle animation

entries.t: Ink streamlines in a curl-noise wind
entries.u: generative-art backgrounds, wind/hair/water/fabric metaphors, "data stream" abstractions; calm and expensive-looking
oscilloscope/audio/retro-tech looks, "signals", a continuously evolving abstract centrepiece
friendly, modern product backgrounds, calm hero scenes, "liquid" brand feels; sits under type without competing

entries.t: Pop-art rays behind a hero word
entries.u: bold/playful/retro-pop styles, "announcement" moments, sale/launch/hero-word beats; rotates slowly, scales with a punch on the hit

entries.t: A line that draws itself (SVG path draw-on)
entries.u: arrows/connections, underlines, signatures, route lines, "this leads to that"; one of the most satisfying primitives in motion design
"building up" stories, data-as-architecture, clean explainer visuals with depth but no 3D engine

entries.t: A grid bent by gravity wells
entries.u: tech/physics/"attention" backgrounds; a field being disturbed by a moving point (cursor, planet, signal)
music/voice/podcast scenes, logos that "breathe" with sound; with real audio use `K.audioData()` envelopes (see sound.md) instead of noise
handmade/craft/children/storybook tones — the antidote to glossy tech; feels tactile because every layer casts a soft shadow
playful/social/Gen-Z tones, feature highlights as "stickers", reaction bursts; the white outline + soft shadow is what makes shapes read as stickers
fill-the-screen transitions, loading, "level up", water/ocean/emotion metaphors; a rising wave is also a great wipe because it reveals the next scene behind it

entries.t: A dotted globe with glowing arcs between cities
entries.u: "worldwide", "any language", networks, travel, shipping, social reach — the shape people recognise instantly. Dots make the land without map data, the slow turn gives cheap convincing 3D, arcs between pins say "connection"

entries.t: A bold flat-poster system (colour blocks, condensed caps)
entries.u: person / brand intros, promos, menus, event announcements — anything that should feel confident, friendly and designed rather than "techy"
any scene that needs a pictogram (skills, features, facts, menu items): `MG.icon(g, name, x, y, size, color, p)` with p = 0…1, 50 built-in icons (`MG.icons`)
the glue of every motion-graphics film: the scene changes while a coloured shape covers the frame (`wipe` per scene in the spec)
whenever the first idea feels like "a product video". Do it on paper in brief.md: three rungs for the main message

entries.t: One object that transforms through the film
entries.u: gives 15–60 s a spine without dialogue: the viewer follows ONE thing. Works for showreels, brands, explainers

entries.t: The camera that goes where no camera can
entries.u: hooks and transitions; most memorable shots in motion design are impossible camera moves
films under 20 s: a single big contrast is easier to land than a sequence of equally pretty scenes

entries.t: A single continuous camera through every scene
entries.u: showreels and brand films that should feel expensive and connected; "one gesture, many worlds"

entries.t: A typed line becomes a world
entries.u: AI/creation/automation stories: the prompt IS the hero. A caret types a sentence; each word spawns its visual (letters flying out, the scene assembling around the text)

entries.t: Start close, zoom out to the truth
entries.u: surprise reveals ("this tiny thing is part of that giant thing"), scale/community stories
showreels, trailers, "N things" explainers: the editing itself is the idea
problem→solution stories (communication breakdown → clarity): the "problem" is shown as distortion, the product restores it
comparison, translation, dubbing, collaboration, A/B: the frame divides and each half is a world that responds to the other
social-first cuts and logo stings; invites replays; elegant for 8–15 s pieces
subjects about speaking across languages (translation tools, learning apps, subtitles, dubbing, travel)
"instant", "live", "zero delay" claims
AI products. Avoid the cliché blue brain: show *behaviour* (thinking, noticing, choosing) not anatomy
open-source tools: value = many hands, transparency, freedom
privacy-first / offline / on-device claims
showreels, tools for creators, portfolio films
traction, results, impact stories
social products, platforms, communication, communities
heritage, "years of …", emotional films
any "before → after" product benefit
"just works", minimal products, calm brands
international reach, "for everyone"
music, audio, podcast, voice tools, events
résumé/showreel films where the *work is the content* (the first user prompt!). Do not narrate skills — **demonstrate range with one coherent style**
every film: the first 1–2 seconds decide whether anyone watches the next 13
every film: the last 2–3 seconds are what is remembered and shared
epic/serious title reveals, "dawn" moments, anything that should feel important; a black title silhouette against a radiant source
a bright light entering frame (sun, headlight, logo reveal glint); sells "camera" instantly. One pass per hero moment — not constantly
warm, organic, nostalgic or hopeful scenes; between-scene accents; a cheap way to make digital graphics feel like film
reveal content gradually (mystery, stage, "find the detail"), a lens-of-attention metaphor, noir/thriller or theatrical tone
power, shock, "idea!" beats, storm moods, electric transitions, impact of a big reveal
dramatic product/character shots: the object is almost black, defined only by coloured edge light — premium, moody, techy
titles and logos that should look like objects standing on glass; premium/tech feel without 3D
flat/bold graphic styles, icons, sticker-like titles; adds depth without gradients

entries.t: A neon sign that flickers on
entries.u: a brand name or a word in a dark room with a retro / night-city / cyber mood. The ON sequence carries the drama — dead, stutter, steady — and the coloured light it throws on the wall sells the space

entries.t: A dusk landscape with depth: aerial perspective, mist, moon, aurora, fireflies
entries.u: meditative / ambient films, loops, wallpapers, calm openers, "breathing" backgrounds behind a title — anywhere the picture itself is the hero and nothing should shout. Flat silhouettes of the same dark colour look like clip art; this recipe
the classic, punchy sting: the mark drops from large, lands with squash, a ring and sparks leave it, the frame shakes. 1.2 s, works for any mark

entries.t: The mark draws itself, then fills
entries.u: elegant/technical brands; the line draws, the fill fades in, a glint passes. Best for marks built from clean geometry

entries.t: A glint of light crosses the mark
entries.u: premium, calm brands; after the mark has appeared, a soft diagonal band of light passes over it ONLY where the mark is — the finishing touch of most expensive-looking stings
tech/energetic brands; the inverse of an explosion: dozens of tiles fly in from everywhere with spin, scale and stagger, lock into the mark, a flash seals it
corporate/clean intros, "opening" metaphors (doors, curtains, a book), a transition INTO the brand scene
loading → brand ("charging up"), water/drink/energy/wellness brands, progress metaphors. The silhouette is the container

entries.t: Slices and RGB split settle into the mark
entries.u: cyber/tech/gaming/security brands, "signal found" stories; 0.6 s of corruption that resolves into a clean mark on the hit

entries.t: Mark + wordmark lock-up with orbiting accents
entries.u: the end card of almost any film: mark above, name below, a tagline, small accents that keep moving so the hold never goes dead

entries.t: The mark inside a growing light ring (GPU)
entries.u: cinematic stings: a thin ring of light expands from the centre as the mark fades up, anamorphic streaks ride the bloom; works in dark scenes with a coloured accent
friendly/consumer/kids/social brands; bouncy spring scale (`K.spring`), confetti cannons, a wobble on settle

entries.t: A mark that builds itself and a name that pops letter by letter
entries.u: channel / brand intros of 5–8 s (`logo` scene): the mark assembles with an overshoot, three rings pulse out, the name pops letter by letter, a tagline slides up, a shine crosses it
the default "expensive" finish for realistic/3D/city/product scenes; warm highlights, cool shadows, a touch more contrast
serious/dramatic/historical beats, a "memory" scene, a contrast cut against colour scenes
dreamlike, romantic, nostalgic, "memory", fantasy; the visual opposite of noir
trailers, sci-fi, night cities, any scene with bright lights; pair with `Cine.letterbox` bars (2.39:1)
nostalgia, archive footage, "years ago", retro-pop; soft and warm
"the machine's view", code/AI/matrix tones, a hard stylistic cut, turning any scene (3D, particles, UI) into text art; very strong signature technique
retro-computing, poster/print texture, "low-fi" interludes, a bold cut away from smooth gradients
"hand-drawn" feel, history/science/editorial tones, a drawn-by-pen interlude
cathedral/crystal/low-poly looks, "fragments", shatter-in transitions (animate `cells` from 80 down to 10)
found-footage, 80s/90s nostalgia, "recording", flashbacks; short bursts (0.3–0.8 s) are better than a whole film
"on a screen" scenes (terminal, game, old TV), tech-nostalgia; the quick way to make UI look physical
graphic/poster/editorial/pop styles; the opposite of "realistic 3D"; strong with flat colours and big type
force any footage into the brand palette; unify clashing scenes; instant stylisation (3 colours: shadows, mids, highlights)
Tron/cyber/blueprint looks; turns any flat-shaded scene into glowing line art; great on 3D renders and logos
game/retro scenes, "loading", censorship-style reveals (animate `size` 64 → 1 for a pixel-in reveal)
aerial/city/landscape shots that should look like toys; a playful change of scale
ornamental/psychedelic/Persian-pattern feeling from ANY source; transitions ("everything folds into a pattern"); spinning logo backgrounds
playful transitions and emphasis (magnify a detail, twirl away), "drain" effects, hypnotic intros
errors, transitions into chaos, "signal" beats; trigger for 3–8 frames on hits, not continuously
engraved-metal / paper-cut / coin looks from flat artwork; subtle tactility on UI

entries.t: Smoke becomes a word, then another word, then an object
entries.u: brand/logo reveals, "chaos → order" metaphors, translating one word into another (English → Persian is the perfect demo of this engine)
exits and transitions ("it all dissolves into the next scene"), emotional endings, the Thanos snap
the loud beat (logo hit, drop, "boom"), cut on impact, anything that needs a physical exclamation mark
wins, launches, "it worked", birthdays, the end of an explainer's happy path
depth and air behind almost any scene; makes a static background feel photographed; hero/product/quiet moments
dreamy night scenes, "magic", forests, a gentle loop under a title
mood weather, winter/rainy tones, "falling" metaphors (data, letters, stars); rain = long motion-blur streaks, snow = soft slow dots
winter/quiet/emotional moods, "falling" letters or stars, a soft layer over a night-blue gradient or a 3D scene
openers and transitions in space/AI/"universe of data" stories; rotating logo-like object made of light

entries.t: A 3D object made of light points
entries.u: tech/hologram/scan looks, "data object", a model that should feel digital; reveal by morphing from a cloud
a multi-coloured logo/icon/illustration built from light; "pixel" reveals; turning a drawing into a living object

entries.t: A glowing comet with a tapering trail (2D)
entries.u: guiding the eye along a path (from A to B), "signal travels", loading arcs, drawing a connection between two nodes
a cheap, always-pretty background for titles, lower thirds and end cards; "city lights out of focus"

entries.t: One foreground layer over every scene
entries.u: ambient dust/bokeh/sparks that drift across ALL scenes (including during transitions) so the film has one consistent air; the cheapest way to lift every static-ish 2D scene

entries.t: A different slow move for every scene
entries.u: gives every scene its own camera gesture (push, pull-out, drift, roll) without hand-animating each draw function; the single biggest cure for "slideshow" energy warnings

entries.t: Run any 2D scene through a shader filter
entries.u: a scene drawn with canvas 2D that should look like VHS (the "problem" scene), ASCII (the machine's view), a mosaic (shatter-in), a CRT… without rewriting it in GLSL

entries.t: A PNG logo on white becomes a transparent mark (and particles)
entries.u: the client's logo exists only as a PNG on white; you need it on dark backgrounds, glowing, and dissolving into particles

entries.t: Pin 2D beams and labels to a point on a 3D object
entries.u: callouts, laser beams, sound waves entering/leaving a 3D object, HUD labels that follow a rotating model; the engine's depth ordering is 3D-only, so you choose the layering yourself

entries.t: Fake "video" for UI scenes, drawn in code
entries.u: a UI scene needs moving picture inside a player/browser/phone and you have no footage: generate it — a night sky with aurora ribbons, a moon, parallax hills — so the UI looks alive and on-brand; `tint` 0 → grey (an un-translated, meaningles

entries.t: Name every sound-and-picture event in the cues
entries.u: any moment where the picture and the soundtrack must meet exactly — a click, a label pop-in, a logo chime. Hard-coded seconds drift apart the moment you retime a scene

films about translation, two languages, two parties, before/after — give each side a colour and a direction and let EVERY scene be a negotiation between them (e.g. violet = source, enters left→right; cyan = target, enters right→left; the lo
choose a mood in one line; every scene needs a background that is not flat black. `FX.bgs` lists names, `FX.info(name).desc` says what the four colours mean
an abstract hero object with no mesh: merging liquid-metal blobs; "fluid", "alive", "melting" ideas; backgrounds behind a title
"network", "cells", glass shatter, cracked earth/lava, a restless tech background
psychedelic/"infinite" transitions, science/maths tone, a hypnotic loop under a title. Smooth colouring (no banding) is what makes it look expensive
a graphic, rhythmic background; maze/flow/"connections" metaphors; Islamic-inspired interlace feel without heavy geometry

entries.t: Morphing SDF shape with ripple contours
entries.u: calm abstract graphics, logo-adjacent backgrounds, "pulse/ripple" under a title, an elegant way to morph circle → square → star
speed ramps, transitions into "the future", scene changes in sci-fi/tech tones, loading screens that aren't boring

entries.t: Striped sun over a perspective grid
entries.u: 80s/synthwave/music tones, "going somewhere", a ready-made hero background that needs only a title over it

entries.t: Water rings that bend a pattern
entries.u: a drop/tap/click moment, "signal spreads", sound waves, calm product backgrounds; the ripples also distort whatever you draw under them (use the same maths on a texture UV)

entries.t: Closed-form motion blur by sampling time
entries.u: ANY fast-moving shader/graphic: instead of feedback buffers (forbidden: frames are independent), evaluate the scene at N times inside the shutter window and average. Same idea powers `Parts` motion blur and the renderer's `--blur`
playful/graphic/print looks (riso, comic, poster), a bold light background that is not another dark gradient

entries.t: The logo hit (layers that make a hit feel big)
entries.u: the loudest moment of the film: a logo/word landing, the "drop", the reveal. A single `impact` is thin — stack: riser → silence → impact + sub + click + chime + pad

entries.t: Tick, pop, type, swipe, success, error
entries.u: every interface moment: cursor clicks, typing, toasts, toggles, results. Sync each to the exact frame of the visual (read the time from the same cue)
under every fast move and transition (whip, slide, zoom): start the whoosh ~0.3 s BEFORE the cut so its peak lands on it
the structure of almost every good 15–30 s video: 2–4 s of rising tension, 0.1–0.3 s of near-silence, then the drop (groove + hit)
under glitch transitions, data/hacker moments, "system" beats; short bursts (0.15–0.4 s) at cut points
suspense, "something is about to happen", emotional or serious moments; the opposite of a groove
confident, forward-moving product/tech/launch films at 120–128 BPM; the default "modern" energy
urban/modern/streetwear/sport reels; heavy sub, snappy rolling hi-hats, snare on beat 3
fast cuts, chase/race/"speed" themes, high-energy montages (170 BPM feel at tempo 170; here 120 BPM breakbeat)
calm, friendly, "everyday" or reflective films at 70–90 BPM; a warm bed under voice-over

films for Persian audiences or any film that should feel Iranian/Middle-Eastern: celebrations, heritage + technology, Nowruz-like warmth. An approximation of the idiom — a native musician will refine it

entries.t: A Shur phrase on santur with ney drone
entries.u: a lyrical Persian theme: openers, emotional beats, endings. Quarter-tones give the character: `'Ed4'` = E lowered by a quarter tone (koron), `'E+4'` = raised (sori)
openers, emotional beats, quiet-to-loud arcs; the sound of "something important is beginning"
neon/retro/night-city/tech scenes; a forward-moving melodic bed with echo
the last 3 seconds: the chord resolves to major/open, bells shimmer, everything rings out into reverb — a sound people remember as "the end"
under quiet establishing shots, nature/space/meditative films; fills silence with life so the mix never goes dead

a "person talking" bed when you have no voice-over (translation/dubbing demos: one babble in a dull timbre for the original, a brighter one for the dub); never use as a substitute for real narration if the story depends on words

entries.t: Music mood and sound design from the same spec
entries.u: scoring a motion-graphics film without hand-placing a single sound: `mood` (upbeat · chill · tech · cinematic) chooses chords, groove, bass and keys; every scene start gets a whoosh + thud, every item a pop (same time formula as the picture
product/brand/tech films that should feel expensive and powerful; the cinema template

stories, education, kids, wellness, food — warm and human

consumer apps, social, kids, campaigns for young audiences
serious subjects, documentary, journalism, luxury/heritage with restraint
science, AI "intelligence", big ideas, global scale, inspirational films
reports, growth stories, analytics, civic/finance explainers
poetry, culture, mindfulness, craft, arts; very Persian-friendly with Nastaliq/Ruqaa
security, techno, gaming, rebellious brands, "system failure" stories
lifestyle, community, friendly brands, wellness, "good vibes"

entries.t: Puffy chrome word on a glossy floor
entries.u: THE hero shot — brand name / title as a polished 3D object; opening or end card; works for Persian (`Geo.text('سلام')`)

entries.t: Faceted glass jewels refracting the sky
entries.u: premium/luxury, "clarity", crystals, abstract hero objects, end-card ornaments
showing "range", a brand-material moodboard, choosing a look; a rotating nine-ball shot is also a strong abstract hero
tech/scale/ambition beats, "the world", a travelling scene between two ideas; the single most cinematic 3D shot you can get cheaply

entries.t: Wireframe terrain under a low sun
entries.u: retro-future, music, "journey", data landscapes; wireframe = abstract and cheap, no textures needed
a "system" or "platform" metaphor, loading/processing, planet/atom look, background for a title

entries.t: Fly through a tunnel of glowing rings
entries.u: speed, transition between sections, "going deeper", music drops, loading → reveal
biology/data/flow metaphors, abstract hero, "two things intertwined" (two languages, two people)
turn a logo/glyph/icon into a metal object without a 3D model; seals, coins, emblems; end cards

entries.t: A live 2D interface mapped onto a 3D device
entries.u: app demos with a camera move (the 2D UI stays pixel-perfect and animated while the phone tilts/orbits); "feature" shots

entries.t: Planet with glowing atmosphere and moon
entries.u: scale, "global" ideas (translation between countries!), science/space, night-sky openers
rhythm/data/"many voices" metaphors, beat-synced backgrounds (drive the wave with hits), abstract skylines
calm, nature, "peaceful", children/indie tones; a dreamy alternative to neon cities
product reveals, "the thing itself" shots, trophies/vases/bottles; `Geo.lathe` turns a 2D profile into a bottle, vase, chess piece, lamp

entries.t: A hero ring in brushed titanium: macro camera, coloured light pools, exploded view
entries.u: launch films for a physical object (smart ring, watch band, bracelet, a washer-shaped part); any "the thing itself" shot where a 2D outline would look cheap; the exploded view (`ex` 0 → 1) is the "what's inside" beat
sci-fi interfaces, "analysis", blueprint/AI/network tones, anything that should feel digital rather than physical

entries.t: The 32 GPU transitions (what each one means)
entries.u: pick by meaning — energetic: whip · zoomBlurCut · zoom · spin · slide · glitch · flash · scan · slice  /  graphic: iris · diamond · clock · spiral · blinds · checker · dots · doors · flip · wipe · luma  /  organic: dissolve · burn · ink · l

entries.t: Write your own transition in 5 lines
entries.u: when none of the 32 says what you mean — a brand-shaped wipe, diagonal stripes, a logo-shaped iris. Your transition then works in Stage (`enter: ['stripes', .6]`) like a built-in
a shape in scene A *becomes* scene B (a sun, a button, an eye, a logo dot grows into the next scene) — the match cut, the most elegant way to change scenes
bold, graphic, brand-coloured cuts (explainers, social, motion-design reels); the panel colours should come from the palette

entries.t: Fall into A, emerge from B (2D)
entries.u: "going deeper", entering a screen/world, tech and dream tones; pairs with a whoosh and a hit
UI/explainer tone, calm and clear ("next step"), carousels; the depth cue (A moves slower, B casts a shadow) makes it feel like layers instead of a flat slide

entries.t: Flash + shake + split on a hit (2D)
entries.u: the cut that lands on a drum hit; logo slams; section starts of a track. Most "pro" cuts are this: a 3–5 frame accent, not a long effect
the big statement; a tagline that fills the frame; "headline" beats of 1.5–3 s

entries.t: One word per beat, slammed in
entries.u: hook sequences ("THIS. IS. NOT. A SLIDESHOW."), lyric-video energy, countdowns
a single powerful word, music-poster look ("RHYTHM RHYTHM RHYTHM"), section titles

entries.t: Lines rise out of invisible masks

entries.t: Slices fly in and snap together

calm/premium moods, "alive" idle text, emphasis without moving the layout much
friendly/joyful tone, "flow" words (music, ocean, motion); a bridge between two statements
"access granted", loading → result, tech/security tone, turning gibberish into meaning (a perfect noise → signal metaphor)
quiet, human moments; chat/code/search-box scenes; punchline after silence

entries.t: Letters as a window onto anything
entries.u: a huge word filled with moving colour, a shader frame, a photo or video; the "title over nothing" look
rotating badges/seals, "sticker" accents, logo lock-ups, a decorative spinning ring around a hero
stats ("12M users"), prices, progress, countdowns; the most convincing "numbers going up" move

entries.t: Letters fly in and snap together
entries.u: logo/name reveal with energy, "everything comes together" metaphors, end cards
nightlife/synthwave/cyber tones, "open" signs, a title that needs a warm electric glow
subtitles with presence, voice-over line reveals, lyric/explainer lines

entries.t: Twelve bundled fonts and what each is for
entries.u: pick fonts BEFORE designing — type choice is half of a style system. Specimen: `references/gallery/fonts.jpg` / `examples/fonts.html`

entries.t: Poetic Persian title (Nastaliq) with a quiet gold glow
entries.u: heritage/poetry/literary tones, openers and end cards for Persian audiences; a refined contrast to techy sans type. Pair with `gfx-girih-reveal` or `particles-dust-ambient`

subtitles that are part of the design — captioned products, lyric videos, spoken explainers. The active word lights up, the others wait, a pill glides from word to word; the line is readable the whole time

entries.t: Text that writes itself (outline, pen glow, then fill)
entries.u: elegant titles, poetry in Nastaliq, a signature or brand name — a glowing pen head travels along the word, leaving a thin outline that turns into the solid word a beat later. Reads as "crafted", costs nothing

entries.t: Lines that slide up out of a mask
entries.u: titles, names, quotes, sub-lines — the default entrance for any line of text in a designed film (`MG.mask`)

entries.t: Numbers that count up inside cards
entries.u: "8+ years · 120 projects · 14 awards", prices, percentages — numbers are the strongest thing a simple film can show (`stats` scene, `MG.stat`)

entries.t: Four ways for a line to arrive
entries.u: titles and big words where one entrance for every line looks like a template: `"styles": ["slideL", "slam"]` on a title scene, or `style` on `MG.mask`

entries.t: Type, click, result (with a real cursor)
entries.u: the core of any product explainer: "describe it → press Render → result appears"; shows the product doing its job in 4 seconds
communication products, social proof, "two people, two scripts" (mix Persian and English bubbles); the typing indicator builds anticipation

entries.t: Code being typed with syntax colours
entries.u: developer/open-source/API stories ("it's just three lines"), tutorials; makes abstract capabilities concrete
growth/metrics stories, "it works" evidence; three numbers + one chart is the whole language of data in 4 seconds
"things happening in real time" (messages, payments, renders finishing), social-proof moments, phone lock-screen looks

entries.t: Frosted glass cards over a living background
entries.u: modern, premium UI looks; floating cards over a colourful shader background; feature grids

entries.t: Ring progress with a big number
entries.u: "98 % accuracy", loading/processing, shares, completion; a ring + number is instantly readable
any story about voice, speech, music, dubbing, podcasts; the waveform is the universal "sound" glyph; here it turns into subtitle text (voice → words)
"everything is connected", communities, servers, supply chains; signals travelling along edges read as live data
"customise everything", feature lists as live controls, privacy/settings stories; each toggle flips on a beat for rhythm

entries.t: "73 of 100": a grid of people that fills to a statistic
entries.u: ONE statistic that must be felt, not read — "7 of 10 …", "1 in 4 …". The grid makes the number physical; the counter and one headline do the rest. Place it in the middle third of an explainer
a menu with prices, a schedule, three speakers with talk titles, steps (`list` scene)

entries.t: One icon, one number, one sentence
entries.u: each fact of an infographic or explainer (`fact` scene): a colour flood, one big self-drawing icon in rings, one counting number, one sentence

entries.t: Bars, ring or line with the key value highlighted
entries.u: a comparison or a progress value (`chart` scene): bars grow with outExpo, a ring fills to its percent, a line draws left to right
